labels.name: Sokan (performing rights organization, for copyright registration)

podcast.title: Bafflement at Rediscovery
podcast.body: When Chris Booth learned about the extensive online search for his song, he was completely baffled by the attention. He considered officially releasing it but faced challenges, as he no longer possessed all the constituent parts of the song (like guitar and synth pieces) and the master recording was with a deceased friend. "When news of the search and mystery reached Chris, he was completely baffled."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Composing for Porn Films
podcast.body: Christopher St. Booth, after his band Sweeny Todd broke up, moved to Encino, California, and took on odd jobs. When offered an opportunity by a friend who made porn films, he started writing music for them due to the good money, carefully registering the copyrights with Sokan, the Canadian Performing Arts Organization. "Then, a friend who made porn said, I need music for one of my new films. Can you do it? Sure they can."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lost Song Discovered in Porn Film
podcast.body: The song "Alter Your Motives" (known as "Everyone Knows That" during its search) was found within an obscure 1986 porn film titled "Angels of Passion" by online music detectives. The "carnal noises" from the film were removed by fans, not the original creators, to isolate the music. "The searchers then watched every porn film featuring Chris Booth's music until they found the song in an obscure movie from 1986 called Angels of Passion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Porn Film Career
podcast.body: After 1986, Christopher St. Booth and his twin brother Philip Booth shifted their focus from porn film music to specializing in movies about ghosts and exorcisms. "Well they went on to specialize in movies about ghosts and exorcisms."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Breakup
xref.body: The band Sweeny Todd disbanded in 1978, leading its members, including Christopher St. Booth and his twin brother Philip Adrian Booth, to pursue other ventures. "Swini Todd broke up in 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
